issue.title: Rust agent scans drop process_identity, so the PID-reuse guard degrades to PID-only for scanned records
issue.description:
Proposed by phase sase-1om.1 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #1) of epic sase-1om. Landing agent
sase-1om.land confirmed it at sase-core 16a3ed0: nothing under
`crates/sase_core/src/agent_scan/` mentions `process_identity`.

## Defect

The Python scan-wire mirrors declare `process_identity` on agent_meta and on the running
marker (src/sase/core/agent_scan_wire_markers.py), and the liveness probes read it:
`record_liveness_probe` in src/sase/core/runner_slots/_scan.py and the listing probe in
src/sase/agent/_running_listing_common.py. The Rust agent scan (`scanner.rs` / `wire.rs`)
never projects the generic `process_identity`, so a real scan of metadata containing,
for example, `boot:99` returns None. Only the monitor-specific `supervisor_identity` is
projected; roster-fixes (sase-1om.1) uses it to keep reused-PID exclusion for monitors.

## Impact

For every non-monitor record that comes from a Rust scan, including admission's
`runner_slots.scan.json` cache, `sase agent list`, and the machine capacity report, the
PID-reuse guard silently degrades to a PID-only check. A dead agent whose PID was reused
can look live and hold phantom runner capacity.

## Fix sketch

Project `process_identity` from agent_meta.json and the RUNNING marker in the sase-core
agent scan wire and scanner, update the binding round-trip tests, and decide whether
existing artifact-index payloads need a refresh or a schema bump so indexed records gain
the field. Move sase's `sase-core-revision.txt` pin past the core commit (see
docs/rust_backend.md), and add a sase-side test that a scanned record carries the
identity through to the liveness probe.
